text:
A fifth-round pick from 2019 who spent last season scoring 38 points for San Diego in the AHL, Judd Caulfield made his NHL debut this fall at 25 and has become a regular. NHL.com's Rookie Watch this week had him "earning trust" with Anaheim, and the ice time agrees: about 14:30 a night lately, up two minutes, with four of his nine points on the power play.

The way he plays is easy to describe. He hits everybody (59 hits in 17 games) and he goes to the net. His shot isn't hard, 72 mph at the top, 10th percentile on NHL EDGE, but his chances are good: 1.35 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his own chances). Four goals on 5.2 expected says he has, if anything, finished a little below his looks.

The caution is his on-ice numbers. Anaheim has scored about four more goals than expected with him out there, and at five-on-five the Ducks take 47% of the expected goals in his minutes. That's still better than they manage without him.

Seventeen games is a small sample. The thing to watch is whether the chances keep coming as the minutes grow.
